nodes.summary: The coordinate process under the existing canonical matrix-derived Markov law satisfies the original finite-state Markov-chain specification on `Filtration.piLE`.
nodes.title: Canonical Markov law satisfies the finite Markov chain specification

nodes.summary: For $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and a history $x = (x_0, \dots, x_a)$ of states in $S$, indexed by $\{0, \dots, a\}$, the last-coordinate history of $x$ is the history indexed by $\{0\}$ whose only entry is $x_a$.
nodes.title: Last-coordinate history

nodes.title: Markov property of the canonical Markov chain measure

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a Markov kernel from a measurable space $S$ to itself and let $\mu$ be a measure on $S$. Under the canonical Markov chain measure $P_\mu$ on $S^{\mathbb{N}}$ with initial measure $\mu$ and transition kernel $\kappa$, the law of the initial coordinate is $\mu$: the pushforward of $P_\mu$ along $\omega \mapsto \omega_0$ equals $\mu$.
nodes.title: Initial distribution of the canonical Markov chain measure

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a Markov kernel from a measurable space $S$ to itself and let $\mu$ be a measure on $S$. The canonical Markov chain measure $P_\mu$ is the measure on the path space $S^{\mathbb{N}}$ given by the Ionescu–Tulcea theorem for the initial measure $\mu$ and, at each time $n$, the kernel sending a history $(x_0, \dots, x_n)$ to $\kappa(x_n, \cdot)$. When $\mu$ is a probability measure, $P_\mu$ is the law…
nodes.title: Canonical Markov chain measure

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a Markov kernel on $S$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $x = (x_0, \dots, x_n)$ a history of states in $S$. The law on path space of the Markov chain with transition kernel $\kappa$ and initial distribution the Dirac measure at $x_n$ equals the Ionescu–Tulcea trajectory measure on $S^{\mathbb{N}}$ started at time $0$ from the one-entry history $(x_n)$ (the last-coordinate history of $x$), in which each next…
nodes.title: Path measure from a point as a trajectory measure

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $S$ and a Markov kernel $\kappa$ on $S$, the path measure $P_\mu$ is the measure on $S^{\mathbb{N}}$, with the product $\sigma$-algebra, obtained by integrating against $\mu(dx)$ the Ionescu–Tulcea trajectory measure that starts at $x$ at time $0$ and draws each next state from $\kappa$ applied to the current state. It is the Markov chain measure of $\kappa$ and $\mu$; when $\mu$ is a…
nodes.title: Markov chain path measure

nodes.summary: For a Markov kernel $\kappa$ on $S$, a function $Y : S^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbb{R}$ of paths and a state $x \in S$, the expectation $E_x Y$ is the integral of $Y$ against the Markov chain path measure with transition kernel $\kappa$ and initial distribution the Dirac measure at $x$.
nodes.title: Expectation under the chain started from a point

nodes.summary: For a kernel $\kappa$ on $S$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the kernel from histories $(x_0, \dots, x_n)$ of states in $S$, indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$, to $S$ that sends $(x_0, \dots, x_n)$ to $\kappa(x_n, \cdot)$. It is the Markov lift kernel of $\kappa$ at $n$.
nodes.title: Lifted transition kernel on histories

nodes.summary: For a kernel $\kappa$ from a measurable space $S$ to itself and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the lifted kernel from $S^{\{0, \dots, n\}}$ to $S$ sends a history $(x_0, \dots, x_n)$ to $\kappa(x_n, \cdot)$: it reads off the last coordinate and applies $\kappa$.
nodes.title: Lifting a kernel to histories

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a nonempty standard Borel space, $\kappa$ a Markov kernel on $S$, and $Y : S^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbb{R}$ a bounded function, measurable for the product $\sigma$-algebra. Then the map $x \mapsto E_x Y$, sending a state $x$ to the expectation of $Y$ under the Markov chain with transition kernel $\kappa$ started from $x$, is measurable.
nodes.title: Measurability of the Markov expectation

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a Markov kernel on $S$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$. For a history $x = (x_0, \dots, x_a)$ of states in $S$, let $Q_x$ be the law of the history $(X_0, \dots, X_{a+b})$ that equals $x$ at times $0, \dots, a$ and then draws each next state from $\kappa$ applied to the current state (the Ionescu–Tulcea partial trajectory from time $a$ to time $a + b$). nodes.title: Shifted finite-dimensional distributions

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a Markov kernel on $S$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$. For a history $z = (z_0, \dots, z_{a+b})$ of states in $S$, extend $z$ by one step, drawing $z_{a+b+1}$ from $\kappa(z_{a+b}, \cdot)$, and then keep the entries at times $a, \dots, a + b + 1$, reindexed as $0, \dots, b + 1$. nodes.title: One-step shift of the partial trajectory kernel

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a Markov kernel on a measurable space $S$, let $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $z = (z_0, \dots, z_{a+b})$ be a history in $S^{\{0, \dots, a+b\}}$. Let $\mu_z$ be the one-step partial trajectory of the lifted kernel of $\kappa$ from time $a + b$ to time $a + b + 1$ started at $z$, that is, the law of $(z_0, \dots, z_{a+b}, X)$ where $X$ has law $\kappa(z_{a+b})$. Then the image of $\mu_z$ under the…
nodes.title: One-step shift of a Markov partial trajectory

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a measurable space. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th σ-algebra of the path filtration on $S^{\mathbb{N}}$, generated by the coordinate maps $\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ for $i \le n$, is contained in the product σ-algebra on $S^{\mathbb{N}}$.
nodes.title: The path filtration is contained in the product σ-algebra

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a measurable space. The path filtration on the path space $S^{\mathbb{N}}$ is the filtration indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, relative to the product σ-algebra, whose σ-algebra at time $n$ is the one generated by the coordinate maps $\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ for $i \le n$.
nodes.title: Path filtration

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a set and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. The time-$n$ shift on the path space $S^{\mathbb{N}}$ sends a path $\omega$ to the path $k \mapsto \omega_{n+k}$.
nodes.title: Time shift on path space

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a Markov kernel on a measurable space $S$, let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_n) \in S^{\{0, \dots, n\}}$. Let $P_x$ be the trajectory measure on $S^{\mathbb{N}}$ of the lifted kernel of $\kappa$ started at time $n$ from the history $x$, and let $P_{x_n}$ be the trajectory measure of the lifted kernel started at time $0$ from the one-point history $x_n$. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
